**Welcome to the Data Visualization in R Workshop!**


This is a **hands-on** workshop. You'll spend most of the day writing R code and
building plots yourself — from your very first `ggplot()` to an interactive
figure — all on a **real dataset you download at the start**. We keep the theory
short and get you doing things fast.

**By the end you will be able to**

- Download a real dataset and explore it in R
- Build plots with the ggplot2 grammar: *data → aesthetics → geoms → layers*
- Customise plots with colour, shape, size, facets and themes
- Make plots interactive with plotly
- Use an **AI assistant** to write, explain and debug R code — and check what it gives you

:::boxy
New to R or ggplot2? You're in the right place — we build up from zero.
Already comfortable? The **one-hour challenge** at the end will stretch you.
:::

:::boxy
You can also visit the [Data Visualization in Python](https://biosustain.github.io/dsp_workshop_dataviz_python/)
:::

## Choose your setup {-}

Pick whichever suits you — all three lead to the same exercises.

### ☁️ 1. In the cloud (nothing to install) {-}

Run everything in your browser with GitHub Codespaces. Best if you don't want to
install anything.

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/biosustain/dsp_workshop_datavizR)

### 💻 2. On your own computer {-}

Prefer working locally? Install R and RStudio, then install the required packages below.
You'll keep everything you build after the workshop.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# List of required CRAN packages
packages <- c(
  "dplyr",
  "ggplot2",
  "ggrepel",
  "RColorBrewer",
  "rmarkdown",
  "tidyr",
  "plotly"
)

# Install missing packages
install_if_missing <- function(pkg) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org/")
  } else {
    message(pkg, " already installed.")
  }
}

# Run installation
invisible(lapply(packages, install_if_missing))

message("All requested R packages are installed and ready to use!")

```

### 🤖 3. With an AI assistant {-}

Whichever setup you use above, you're **welcome (and encouraged) to use an AI
assistant** — [Claude](https://claude.ai), [ChatGPT](https://chat.openai.com),
or [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot) inside your editor —
as a coding partner throughout the day. See the next section for how to get the
most out of it.

## Using AI in this workshop {-}

AI assistants are great for learning R: they explain error messages, suggest the
next line, and help you iterate on a plot much faster. We treat them as a normal
part of the toolkit — not cheating.

**Good things to ask an AI**

- *"Explain this R error and how to fix it: `<paste error>`"*
- *"Write ggplot2 code to plot `x` vs `y` coloured by `group` from a data frame called `data`."*
- *"How do I make this ggplot interactive with plotly?"*
- *"What does `aes()` do here, in simple terms?"*

:::boxy
**Three rules when using AI**

1. **Run it and read it** — never paste code you don't understand. Ask the AI to
   explain anything unclear.
2. **Check the output** — AI can invent column names or functions. If a plot
   looks wrong, it probably is.
3. **Learn from it** — the goal is that *you* can do it next time, with or
   without the AI.
:::

Look out for **🤖 Ask your AI** tips in the exercises — small prompts you can try.
